problem:
The standard matrix $T$ of a linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{3}$ are given below. Determine if there exists a vector $x\in {R}^{3}$ such that $T(x)=b.$
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2},$ where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ are the components of $x.$  

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 4 \\ -2 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -28 \\ 26\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
Since $T$ is the standard matix of $T,$ we have $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Col}(T).$ In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Im}(T),$ we need to check if the equation $Tx=b$ is consistent. 

So, we find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[T\,|\,b],$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -5 \\ 4 & 2 & 4 & -28 \\ -2 & -4 & 4 & 26\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & -8 \\ 0 & -4 & 8 & 16\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Hence ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. Now, from the second equation, we get 

$$
2{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=-8\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-4+2{x}_{3}.
$$

From the first equation we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=-5\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-5-2{x}_{3}.
$$

As a result, the general solution is given by 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-5-2{x}_{3} \\ -4+2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=1$, we have

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

where $T(x)=b.$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-7+(-2)=-9.$
